absent: Allocation and acquisition path for the shared huge zero folio including reference setup and frame assignment.
Deferred split shrinker accounting and reclaim behavior and associated list handling.
Background collapse thread main loop, scan selection, and address space slot management.
Exact numeric values for order masks, flag positions, size thresholds, and reserve bounds.
Shared memory policy attribute and background tunables group contents and defaults.
Event triggers for fault, swap, split, and collapse statistics counters.
Zone, pageblock, and migration type definitions used in reserve sizing.

findings.text: Releasing the shared huge zero reference from an address space is conditional on that space having recorded prior use; spaces without the marker incur no release action.

A global memory tuning helper recomputes the minimum free reserve and refreshes per-zone watermarks, raising the reserve when huge page support is active to preserve headroom for large allocations and falling back to default calculation otherwise.

A lifecycle helper aligns the background collapse thread with current global enablement, starting it when allowed and stopping it when disallowed, waking existing waiters when work remains and refreshing memory reserves in all cases.

Generic flag helpers expose one boolean control backed by a shared flag word, rendering current state as human readable decimal output and accepting only binary values to set or clear the selected bit.

Initialization prepares a dedicated cache for address space tracking entries and establishes default scan budgets and tolerance thresholds derived from huge page size, while destruction releases the cache.

The shared huge zero folio is reclaimable only while a sole reference remains; the accounting hook advertises full huge page capacity in that state and none otherwise, and the reclaim hook succeeds only on exclusive transition from sole to none.

Global transparent huge page policy is encoded by two mutually exclusive bits where presence of the first selects unconditional use, presence of the second selects advisory use, and absence of both selects disabled use.

Defragmentation policy uses exclusive selection among direct, background, combined background or advisory, and advisory triggers, with disabled represented by no selection bit and display marking the active choice.

Per-size anonymous policy maintains exclusive membership of each size in one of unconditional, inherited, or advisory sets, with disabled represented by membership in none and inherited deferring to the global policy.

The huge_zero_lock guard serializes global zero folio pointer and frame identifier updates, pairing atomic reference transitions with detachment so acquisition and reclamation cannot interleave unsafely.

The huge_anon_orders_lock guard serializes updates to the per-size anonymous policy sets so that moving a size between unconditional, inherited, and advisory states appears atomic to concurrent readers.
The khugepaged_mutex guard serializes background thread creation, termination, and wake decisions against concurrent policy changes so thread presence always reflects the latest enablement.

Three small enumerations define policy vocabularies: anonymous per-size ordering from unconditional through inherited and advisory to disabled, global ordering from unconditional through advisory to disabled, and defragmentation ordering from direct through staged and advisory variants to disabled.

Per-processor statistics tables indexed by size and counter kind accumulate transparent huge page events locally, with a summation helper aggregating across all processors for reporting and a generator defining read-only per-size display attributes.

The top-level transparent huge page attribute set groups global controls for enablement, defragmentation, zero page use, huge page size reporting, shared memory policy when configured, and underused reclamation, each with appropriate read or read-write access.

Per-size control hierarchy provides distinct groups for anonymous, file-backed, and generic kinds, with anonymous offering an enablement attribute, file offering shared memory policy when configured, and generic remaining empty, all bound to a common object type with custom release handling.

Per-size statistics hierarchy exposes separate named collections for anonymous, file-backed, and generic events, covering allocation outcomes, fallback causes, swap interactions where applicable, split activity, and collapse success or failure.

Sized transparent huge page directory objects are created per supported block size with names derived from byte size, layered with generic then kind-specific control and statistics groups, tracked on a global list, and freed through reference release; alternate builds provide no-op setup and teardown.

Global policy transitions accept unconditional, advisory, or disabled requests, update exclusive flag encoding, and on actual change restart background processing while otherwise only refreshing memory reserves; invalid spellings are rejected.

Defragmentation selection moves exclusively between direct, staged, combined, advisory, and disabled states based on recognized spellings, clearing all other selections on each accepted write and rejecting unrecognized input.

Each anonymous size independently transitions among unconditional, inherited, advisory, and disabled states via recognized spellings, triggering background processing restart on effective change and reserve refresh otherwise, with invalid input rejected.

Overall initialization proceeds from capability check through interface creation, background subsystem setup, and shrinker registration, then enables background processing unless memory is constrained, unwinding prior stages in reverse order on any failure.

User control enters through a dedicated transparent huge page directory offering global enablement, defragmentation, zero page use, size reporting, and reclamation attributes, plus per-size subdirectories for fine-grained policy and statistics.
Early boot configuration accepts unconditional, advisory, or disabled spellings to preset global policy flags before initialization, warning and ignoring absent or unrecognized values.
Memory pressure entry occurs through registered count and scan hooks for deferred splits and for the shared zero folio, installed during initialization and released symmetrically during teardown.

If concurrent acquisition retains the zero folio during reclamation, the reclaim attempt aborts without progress, and a missing folio during exclusive takeover triggers a one-time diagnostic while still detaching global references safely.

Partial initialization failures require careful unwinding of interface objects, background resources, and shrinker registrations to avoid leaks or dangling directories, with distinct handling for interface, subsystem, and shrinker failure points.

Systems below a low-memory threshold default to disabled policy to avoid excess reservation, while policy writes that cause no effective change still refresh reserves to preserve historical watermark behavior.
Global enablement uses stable spellings always, madvise, and never for unconditional, advisory, and disabled policies.
Per-size anonymous enablement adds inherit to the global vocabulary, yielding always, inherit, madvise, and never selections.
Defragmentation uses always, defer, defer+madvise, madvise, and never to select direct, staged, combined, advisory, and disabled behaviors.
Boolean controls use_zero_page and shrink_underused accept binary settings and report decimal state, while hpage_pmd_size reports the fixed huge page byte size.
Reclaim accounting and background defaults scale with HPAGE_PMD_NR and HPAGE_PMD_SIZE, and per-size directory names encode kilobyte sizes derived from page order.
